sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) – free movement of capital and establishment
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties (approximately 100 BITs worldwide)
DTAAs concluded by Luxembourg with more than 80 states, including the US, China, Germany, France, and the UK
EU association and free trade agreements applicable to third-country investors

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 April 2019 on RBE filing procedures; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (SCSp introduced by Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS/LBR); CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, C-37/20 and C-601/20, restricting public UBO access.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (full public access annulled post-CJEU; disclosure to competent authorities and on duly justified legitimate-interest application only)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract or certificate of incorporation of each corporate partner (e.g., the General Partner entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or companies registry of the partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization for non-Hague-Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all proposed UBOs, general partners, and authorized managers
Proof of residential or registered address (recent utility bill or bank statement, less than 3 months old)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the business reputation and account conduct of the partners
Certificate of good conduct / police clearance certificate (casier judiciaire extract) for each manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police authority of the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02: (i) all UBOs, directors, general partners, and authorized signatories must be screened before incorporation against the UN consolidated sanctions list, EU restrictive measures (Regulations 765/2006, 269/2014, and country-specific regimes), Luxembourg national sanctions list, FATF high-risk jurisdictions, and, at banking level, the OFAC SDN list; (ii) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger Enhanced Due Diligence requiring senior-management approval, documented source-of-wealth verification, and continuous 24/7 transaction monitoring; (iii) adverse-media and sanctions-list screening must be repeated at incorporation filing and on any change of UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS electronic portal, www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory registrations and filings are made in French; the company name may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another Latin-script language; non-Latin scripts require a French transliteration in the articles of partnership; the name must be distinctive (non-confusing) against existing RCS entries, must not breach public order, and must carry the corporate form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société Nationale de Crédit et d'Investissement
words implying government sponsorship or regulated financial activities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the LBR/RCS registrar, counsel files a formal administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) with the Ministry of Justice within 30 days of the refusal; a second-instance appeal lies to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Administrative Chamber) within 3 months of the ministerial decision; an amended name may be refiled immediately without prejudice to the appeal; a refused name remains blocked for 3 months to prevent circumvention.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as registered-office domiciliation through a CSSF-approved domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999. For the bonded-warehouse wholesale trade of wines and spirits, physical storage premises in Luxembourg are statutorily mandatory for the excise/customs warehouse licence; a purely virtual registered office without licensed physical substance will fail customs and excise (Douanes et Accises) approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (70%) for the registered office and administrative seat within the first year (RBE, CSSF, and tax authorities verify substance); mandatory (100%) pre-licensing physical inspection of the bonded warehouse by Douanes et Accises and the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 198-1 to 198-10 and 208-1 to 208-2 (Société en Commandite Spéciale); Civil Code provisions on partnership contracts; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts / Acte de Société) executed by notarial deed (Acte notarié) and filed with the RCS; publication in the Electronic Collection of Legal and Administrative Acts (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations – RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital requirement for a SCSp. Partnership interests are freely determined by the Partners and may be subscribed in cash or in kind. No escrow account is statutorily mandated; however, the competent customs and excise authority will require a customs bond or bank guarantee (typically EUR 150,000 to EUR 500,000) for bonded wine/spirit warehouse operations before the excise license is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby subscribe to the partnership interests set forth in the Subscription Schedule, with initial aggregate contributions as agreed, payable in due course upon demand of the General Partner. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at [address] in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as more fully provided in Article 2 of the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name] is appointed as General Partner/Gérant, [name] as Compliance Officer, and [name] as Data Protection Officer, each with authority to open bank accounts, execute regulatory filings, and implement the bonded warehouse licensing plan. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the RCS filing and excise licensing shall be initiated without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – online name reservation service via lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the intended corporate name incorporating either 'SCSp', 'S.C.Sp.', or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. The name must not conflict with an existing registered name, trademark, or contrary to public policy. Provide the proposed legal form, principal activity description (ISIC 4632 bonded wine/spirits wholesale), and the name of the General Partner. The reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (online)
Identity document of the prospective General Partner
Description of corporate object (bonded trade of wines and spirits)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of identity or similarity, file a written appeal with the RCS within 15 days and submit a proposed alternative name referencing registered precedents. If rejected for trademark conflict, obtain a waiver or adjust the name and resubmit immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Signing of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public admitted in Luxembourg (Notaire habilité) – Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene before a Luxembourg notary for execution of the deed of incorporation (Acte de société). The notary must verify the identities and legal capacity of all partners, the General Partner's mandate, the registered office address, capital/subscription schedule, and any in-kind contribution valuation report. For an SCSp, the deed must expressly state that the partnership is an SCSp without legal personality, that the general partner has unlimited liability, and that limited partners have liability limited to their contributions. The notary transmits the deed to the RCS and to the Direct Parcours system (eDesk) for publication.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Subscription schedule (Schedule of Partnership Interests)
Identity documents of General Partner and all Limited Partners
Affidavit of professional address or lease agreement for the registered office
In-kind contribution valuation report (if applicable)
Power of attorney (procuration) for any signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects (e.g. missing valuation report, unclear liability clauses), rectify the draft by written rider and re-execute before the same notary. If the deed is technically rejected by the RCS, a supplementary notarial amendment (acte rectificatif) will be prepared and refiled within the RCS deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – lbr.lu central filing platform; publication by the Luxembourg Official Journal (Mémorial, RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the notary files the incorporation deed and the prescribed statutory forms with the RCS. The RCS assigns a Luxembourg business registration number (numéro RCS). Following admission, the RCS forwards the data for electronic publication in RESA within one month. The filing must include the SCA/SCSp standard information sheet (fichier d'identification), the General Partner's identity, the registered office address, and the corporate purpose aligned with ISIC 4632.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (original or certified copy)
Cross-border information sheet for EU registration (Form 2E, if applicable)
Identification sheet of the General Partner (mandate and signature specimen)
Bank reference of capital account (if any)
Statement by the General Partner accepting legal effectiveness of the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification request, respond within one month with amended deed extracts or explanations; failure to cure leads to deletion of the filing. Use the electronic Téléchargement module to upload corrected documents and reserve rights to appeal under articles 31 and 32 of the RCS law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and VAT / EIN Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD – direct tax authority); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT – registration and VAT authority).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the FISC-1 registration form (for partnerships) to the ACD for the Luxembourg withholding/corporate tax register. Register the SCSp for VAT using the AEDT Electronique Portal (eCDF) by filing Form 3400. The SCSp is eligible for transparent taxation; any direct corporate tax election must be expressly made. For bonded wine/spirit trade, simultaneously lodge the excise registration request to the Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises).
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait du RCS)
Notarial deed of incorporation
Form FISC-1 and VAT registration Form 3400
Proof of registered office (lease title or service provider letter)
Passport copies of General Partner and tax compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Tax registration delays are cured by producing the provisional RCS extract and notarial deed to the ACD physically at once. For VAT number issuance, contact the AEDT taxpayer service by telephone (352-247-40100) and obtain a provisional VAT reference the same day; escalate to the Taxpayer Advisory Board if no response in 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economy – Department of Economic and Commercial Affairs (Ministère de l'Économie, MECO) via the Guichet unique website.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the establishment permit (Autorisation d'établissement) required by the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions. The application covers wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages (wine and spirits) and warehouse operation. The managing General Partner must prove good repute, no prior criminal convictions, and adequate professional competence in beverage wholesale; submit the completed form with educational/professional certificates and a police record extract (bulletin n°2).
required_dossiers: Application for establishment permit (online form via guichet.lu)
Extract from criminal record (bulletin n°2) of the General Partner
Certificates of professional competence (diploma or 3 years full-time experience)
RCS extract and Articles of Association
Lease agreement or ownership title of the warehouse/bonded premises
Site plan of the storage premises and operational facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry questions professional competence, file a dossier of supplementary evidence (course transcripts, employment attestations, supplier references) and request an oral hearing. Decisions may be appealed to the Administrative Court (Tribunal administratif) within 30 days; alternatively, appoint a qualified technical director to meet the competency requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Bonded Warehouse Authorization and Excise License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Authority) – Excise and Movement Directorate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for authorisation as a tax warehouse keeper and for the status of authorised warehousekeeper (entrepôt fiscal) under Excise Directive 2020/262/EU and Luxembourg customs/ excise law. The application must specify the types of excise goods (wine, intermediate products, spirits, ethyl alcohol > 2% abv), the storage capacity, the inventory control system (EMCS-compliant), and the financial bank guarantee. Submit the operational security plan, the emergency firewater containment plan, and the environmental compliance statement. Upon provisional approval, the warehouse is registered in EMCS and authorised to receive bonded consignments.
required_dossiers: Application form for excise warehouse authorisation (Formulaire DA-88)
Evidence of bank guarantee or customs bond (EUR 150,000–500,000)
Site plan, storage tank and vessel list
SOP for stock movement and EMCS e-documentation
Fire safety certification and emergency plan (SID / Luxembourg fire department)
Environmental registration receipt and discharge permit (if applicable)
Notarial deed and RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Customs requires rectifications, the applicant is granted a 30-day cure period to amend security procedures or increase the guarantee. Refusals can be contested before the Minister of Finance within 30 days; a temporary authorization can be sought for limited storage pending full compliance to prevent business interruption.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – Department of Economic and Commercial Affairs (Autorisation d'établissement) jointly with the Administration des douanes et accises for bonded premises and Administration de l'environnement for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement for wholesale trade of alcoholic beverages and operation of a customs bonded warehouse (Entrepôt sous douane) for wines and spirits in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; Excise Tax Warehouse Keeper Licence under EMCS.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg), 1 Rue du Fort Thuengen, L-1499 Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Full Environmental Impact Report (EIA) if warehouse storage aggregate capacity exceeds 50,000 hL or bottling line capacity exceeds 500 hL/day; Category 4 – Registration (simple declaration) for dry warehouse storage of bottled wines and spirits under 10,000 hL; temporary operating permits issued for low-risk warehousing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to surface water must meet EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from spirit/tank storage must satisfy Directive 94/63/EC: annual ethanol storage losses limited to 0.1% of throughput with vapour recovery unit on loading racks; firewater and concentrated spillage (alcohol ≥ 20% v/v) must be contained in a leaktight basin and disposed as hazardous waste under Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management. Soldering, labeling and bottle-washing effluents must respect pH 6.5–9.0 and max. 3 mg/L phenolic compounds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by Service Incendie et Secours (SID) confirming compliance with COT (Commission de la sécurité incendie) regulations for alcohol storage: automatic fire-extinguishing system over tanks > 100 m3, fire hydrant spacing ≤ 50 m, smoke extraction, and firewater containment volume based on largest tank. Structural load inspection certificate from a registered engineer/ bureau de contrôle agréé certifying racking and floor loading at a minimum of 5.0 kN/m2 warehouse capacity. Occupational safety clearance issued by Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering emergency evacuation, handling of ethanol, manual handling risk assessment, and adequate ventilation in cellar/storage areas (ATEX zone classification by SUBROGATION under Luxembourg mining regulations).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities must first obtain a Luxembourg business number (matricule) via RCS registration if carrying on a commercial activity, then file VAT registration with AEDT using Form 645 (or via MyGuichet.lu). For a SCSp without legal personality, the partnership itself registers via the RCS and is allocated a national business number; the tax identification number (TIN) is issued by ACD for direct tax purposes and a separate VAT number by AEDT. A Luxembourg tax representative may be required for non-resident partnerships.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A SCSp is fiscally transparent by default. However, a partnership may elect to be taxed as a body corporate under Article 5(2) LITL if all partners agree and the partnership is deemed to have corporate status for legal purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (transposed into domestic law) apply to recharacterize mismatches; elections are made by written notice to ACD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small enterprise exemption); no threshold for non-resident suppliers performing taxable activities in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 intra-EU distance sales threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg maintains no real-time fiscal clearance model and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing or digital stamping. Electronic invoices in PEPPOL/EU-compliant formats are acceptable. VAT returns and VIES recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu; no real-time API clearance is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods to non-EU destinations where physical departure is proven within the seller's books; to services directly linked to exported goods and performed for a non-EU customer; and to services supplied to a third-country established customer that are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT. Intra-EU supplies are not zero-rated but are reverse-charged in the destination state when the buyer has a valid EU VAT number and the supply is covered by a VIES statement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A) / EU Summary Declaration
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (CMR/AWB)
Inward Remittance Certificate or binding bank proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities (AEDT) may reassess within 5 years (10 years in cases of fraud). Fraudulent zero-rating triggers VAT reassessment, default interest, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 (or four times the evaded tax), criminal penalties up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment under VAT law, and potential suspension or revocation of the bonded warehouse license.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); no separate Foreign Exchange Administration exists. EU exchange-rate and capital-movement rules apply via the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the Euro as legal tender with full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no licensing for ordinary trade payments, and no restrictions on profit or capital repatriation for qualifying pass-through vehicles such as the SCSp, provided transactions do not breach EU/UN financial sanctions, money laundering rules, or UBO disclosure obligations. Remittance hurdles are limited to documentary compliance: proof of underlying commercial transaction, beneficial ownership identification, and statistical reporting through BCL balance-of-payments surveys.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds in Luxembourg. All export receipts may be freely retained, repatriated, or set off against import disbursements. The BCL imposes no conversion ratio and no time limit; however, resident entities must provide periodic balance-of-payments data on cross-border flows exceeding statutory thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus optional Capital Escrow Account for committed subscription instalments
Operational Treasury Account and Bonded Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account and Dedicated Escrow Account for third-party collection or warehouse collateral
Operational Account with ancillary trade finance/LC services; Capital Escrow Account if required by limited partner agreements
Operational Account and Custody/Asset Earmarking Account for bonded inventory pledges

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA licensed Electronic Money Institutions under PSD2. Legal constraints: such EMIs can provide payment accounts and FX execution without full credit institution license, but they are generally unsuitable as primary treasury counterparties for bonded warehouse transactions because they do not offer commercial letters of credit, trade finance, or warehouse receipt financing. Offshore, non-EU/EEA digital EMIs are rated Low or Prohibited for entities holding bonded tax-excise goods due to CSSF AML/CFT expectations requiring a regulated EU bank or licensed EMI with physical or contractual substance, full UBO chain transparency, and audit trail over excise duty status.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: While remote onboarding is legally possible in Luxembourg under CSSF AML/CFT circulars allowing video identification, most Tier-1 commercial banks mandate physical attendance of at least one managing partner (Gérant) or authorised signatory for corporate account opening where a SCSp has non-resident, multi-entity ownership. Where all UBOs are natural persons with clean passports and audited source of wealth, remote digital KYC may be accepted on a case-by-case basis. For any beneficial owner residing in non-FATF or static high-risk jurisdictions, physical presence in Luxembourg is effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through structure with distributed partnership interests and non-resident limited partners located in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart, notarised constitutive deed and limited partnership agreement, CSSF/registre de commerce extract, legal opinion on tax transparency, AML/KYC pack for every direct and indirect beneficial owner above 25% including passport, proof of address, source of wealth statements, corporate registry extracts from jurisdictions of each owner, and an explanation of the unencumbered chain of control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded warehouse trade in high-value alcoholic products creating red flags over excise duty evasion or use for informal value transfer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid customs/excise warehouse authorisation, inventory ledger certified by the bonded warehouse keeper, purchase and sales contracts with real counterparties, transport and insurance documentation, excise duty suspension procedure codes, and a written treasury policy confirming that all payments are made exclusively to invoice-producing third parties with no netting or cash pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately large inbound capital injection from a related corporate undertaking that has no observable operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, board/shareholder resolution approving the capital commitment, deed of contribution and a certified confirmation that the funds originate from an EU-regulated credit institution in a jurisdiction subject to equivalent AML rules, plus source-of-funds tracing from bank statements or a notarised gift/loan document if outside commercial operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to jurisdictions with weak AML enforcement or to bulk-buyer distributors located outside the OECD.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-customer due diligence file including export licences, import permits from the destination country, tax/VAT numbers and customs codes, independent credit rating or bank reference letter, sanctions and PEP screening certificates, incoterms-based invoices, and a written compliance narrative establishing the legitimate movement or sale of goods.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for capital contributions to the SCSp is a SWIFT MT103 by the investor from its bank to the Luxembourg account, referencing the partnership as beneficiary, the SCSp account IBAN and the following remittance info: (a) word 'Capital Contribution' or 'Capital Account Payment'; (b) the ECB Balance-of-Payments purpose code for direct or portfolio investment, commonly 'D' for direct investment or 'A0101' for capital subscription; (c) the notarial or constitutive deed reference; (d) the investor's UBO identifier. Banks may request a signed capital contribution certificate and a copy of the deed. TARGET2 is the intra-EUR clearing rail; SWIFT is used for non-EUR (USD, GBP). Inbound amounts equal to or above EUR 10,000 may trigger CSSF statistical reporting; banks apply standard OFAC and EU sanctions screening on counterparties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For wine and spirits bonded trade, permitted outbound rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 direct transfer for supplier payments, customs duty/VAT payments and warehouse fees; (2) documentary commercial letters of credit (MT700) and standby LCs (MT760) for structured purchases of aged stock; (3) bank payment obligations (BPO) where matched trade data exists; (4) SEPA instant transfers within eurozone for small operational expenses. All outbound disbursements must be supported by invoices, warehouse warrants or delivery orders, and the bank will apply dual-use trade sanctions screening. In EUR, settlement occurs on TARGET2 with irrevocable finality; GBP, USD and other currencies clear through SWIFT with bank correspondent chains. No netting or third-party payments are allowed absent explicit partnership deed authority.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with licensed Luxembourg or EU/EEA investment firms, exec via ISDA or local master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies only where deliverable forwards are unavailable; requires internal policy justification
FX swaps for short-term rolling of receipts into EUR
Cross-currency swaps for term-matched funding or export prepayment structures
Currency options (put/call) for asymmetric protection on major wine-auction and Scotch-export receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 consecutive calendar days after the anniversary date of the original RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extra-judicial fine of up to EUR 250 per missing confirmation; repeated delinquency may trigger RCS strike-off (radiation d'office) and invocation of judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing and Publication (Comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS/RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the annual financial year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end) and subsequent RESA publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and judicial fines ranging from EUR 1,000 to EUR 5,000 may be imposed on the managing partners; persistent non-filing exposes the SCSp to judicial strike-off and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Excise Authorization and Bonded-Warehouse Licence Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal prior to the licence expiry date; LBR/RCS confirmation is required within 15 days of any change to the excise licence particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the bonded-warehouse authorization is immediate upon lapsing; continuation of bonded trade triggers an excise demand, customs penalties up to EUR 1,000, and potential criminal liability of the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises agréé where the SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds: (i) balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; (ii) net turnover EUR 8.8 million; (iii) average 50 employees. In addition, an SCSp operating as an investment vehicle under CSSF oversight must mandatorily appoint an approved statutory auditor irrespective of the quantitative thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and the Commercial Code; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is optional for individual annual accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO form exists, but the Annual Confirmation of Registration requires the SCSp to verify the continuing accuracy of the beneficial-ownership records held by the LBR; any transfer of partnership interests must be notified to the LBR within one month. Deliberate failure to update UBO data is punishable by daily fines up to EUR 250 and custodial sanctions for managing partners; a nil-confirmation procedure is available when the UBO data remain unchanged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Managing Partners / Directors (Registre des gérants)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 4,200 per year for professional registered-office and local administrative agent services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 per year for a bespoke SCSp statutory audit, dependent on transaction volume and transfer-pricing documentation scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT + Luxembourg City municipal business tax coefficient 3.5 yielding 6.72%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and not subject to CIT. For a corporate partner taxed in Luxembourg, the participation exemption exempts substantial shareholdings from CIT (100% exemption on dividends and capital gains). The IP tax box allows an 80% exemption on net IP-derived income. For bonded trade, available deductions: industrial and commercial loss offsets, 20% notional interest deduction (new equity), and investment tax credit applicable to warehousing equipment. No generic tax holidays.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp Tax Transparency Information Return (Déclaration de transparence fiscale) electronically filed via MyGuichet.lu (Guichet unique) in Luxembourg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 December of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end (e.g. FY 31 Dec 2025 -> due 31 Dec 2026); extended to 31 March if filed by a certified chartered accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, LEI (if required), head office address, tax residence confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Luxembourg permanent establishment address; do not list SCSp as tax resident; attach a certificate of residence of the managing general partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, Luxembourg tax number (if applicable), profit/loss sharing ratio, capital account openings and closings, and annual income allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use partner's foreign tax identification number; the SCSp must provide the allocations to non-resident partners for their home-country tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Customs/excise warehouse license number, volume of wine/spirits stored under duty suspension, export and import transaction values.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate if the non-resident partner operates through a Luxembourg fixed place of business; if yes, a Luxembourg tax return is required for the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable double tax treaty articles invoked for each non-resident partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 700 / tax residence certificate if claiming reduced withholding or reporting exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,000 per month, maximum EUR 5,000; late information leading to tax evasion attracts fine up to EUR 25,000 under AO Art 396 and an assessment based on estimated income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax Return (Formulaire 470) on MyGuichet.lu — applicable only to corporate partners receiving SCSp income through a Luxembourg permanent establishment, or if the SCSp has irrevocably elected taxability
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 31 December of the year following the accounting year (standard year 31 Dec); professional tax filers may obtain an extension to 30 April of the second following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, RCS, legal form S.A./S.à r.l./SCSp, tax office and issuing authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner with a Luxembourg PE files this return solely for the PE income sourced from the SCSp.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income computed from the SCSp's financial statements adjusted for non-deductible expenses and participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the PE-attributable share in Box 230; do not include foreign-source income covered by the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholding (>=10% or >= EUR 6 million) deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must hold the participation in the economic interest and meet the 12-month holding condition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and the notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only for tax paid at source in the warehousing jurisdiction and supported by a Form 700/TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing at least EUR 5,000 up to EUR 10,000 plus monthly interest of 0.6% on tax due; deliberate false information by a manager attracts criminal sanctions under AO Art. 397 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders (>=10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost); 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax for portfolio non-resident shareholders not qualifying; 0% on profit distributions by a fiscally transparent SCSp because profits are transparently allocated to partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on a distribution or SCSp profit allocation, the Luxembourg paying agent or SCSp must obtain: (1) an original Form 700 (tax residence certificate) issued by the partner's tax authority in the 12 months preceding payment; (2) a completed Luxembourg tax form 720 (withholding tax rate reduction request); and (3) a statement on the final economic beneficial owner. File with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) at least 15 days before the payment. Retrocessive relief for non-resident partners is available by filing a return within 3 years of the end of the tax year in which income arose. For bonded trade, the DTA article for business profits (e.g. Art. 7 OECD) may fully exempt commission income unless attributable to a Belgian/German PE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 20% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax, reduced to 0% or 5% under most Luxembourg DTAs (e.g. 0% under DTA with China; 5% under DTA with US if beneficial owner); must file Form 720 to access treaty rate. Interest: 0% Luxembourg WHT on corporate-bonded loans and trade debt provided payments are arm's length; however, interests which are not at arm's length or paid to a related tax haven beneficiary may be recharacterised as hidden dividends (15% WHT).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory single local-file threshold. Mandatory Master File / CbCR under Luxembourg CbCR law (EU Directive 2016/881) where the group's consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000. Administrative practice additionally requires a Local File for any SCSp-controlled transaction exceeding EUR 1,000,000 in a tax year, particularly for bonded warehouse licence holders. The local file must include transfer pricing method selection, comparability analysis, and the SCSp's profit allocation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the OECD and EU ATAD general anti-abuse rules. An SCSp conducting bonded wine/spirits trade must demonstrate real economic substance: (i) regular management decisions in Luxembourg, (ii) local bonded warehouse licences and customs declarations, (iii) own office, staff and physical inventory risk, and (iv) compensation commensurate with functions and risks. Under the definition in Luxembourg's Circular L.I.R. n° 100/4, a 'letterbox' SCSp with passive income from spirits trading is disregarded for treaty benefits. Since Luxembourg is not on the EU non-cooperative list, formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) akin to UAE/DFC are not imposed, but the substance requirement is embedded in the arm's length standard and tax residency law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Intentional incorrect income declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring taxable profits or sales from aged wine and spirits bonded trade, or incorrectly characterising inventory disposal as capital gains to avoid CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO) Art. 396-397: fine up to EUR 25,000; an additional fine of 10-25% of the tax evaded; imprisonment for up to 5 years. The tax authorities may issue an estimated assessment without time limit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and the general partner of the SCSp may be jointly and severally liable for the tax evaded if they personally drafted false declarations; travel bans and asset freezes may be ordered; criminal conviction leads to director disqualification of 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp is used as an intermediary in bonded trade without any office, warehouse licence, employees or real commercial decision-making in Luxembourg, creating unreal profits on paper.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration will lift tax transparency and reclassify the profits as Luxembourg-source income subject to CIT + municipal business tax (24.94%) plus 15% dividend WHT upon deemed liquidation. DTA benefits denied and deemed profits assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit letterbox operations are jointly liable for CIT and municipal business tax; the court may pierce the veil under Art. 59 CBCS and order civil damages equal to the revenue authority's legal costs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Excise Duty Evasion under EU Alcohol Warehousing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling duty-suspended spirits without customs stamp, running undisclosed spirits 'bonded transfers' outside the EMCS system, or cash payments for whisky barrels without enhancing due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Luxembourg Customs and Excise Code Art. 57: seizure of goods and vehicles plus fines up to EUR 1,500 per litre of pure alcohol or in any case EUR 250,000; compliance with AML Law of 12 Nov 2004: administrative fine of EUR 250,000 for entities and EUR 1,250,000 for repeat offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual managers face up to 5 years' imprisonment for excise fraud and money laundering, travel bans from Schengen area, confiscation of personal assets, and bank account freezes; professional capacity as board member is lost upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp charges its non-resident parent a below-arm's-length margin on wine or spirit storage/reexports, or fails to document an intra-group licence of the bonded trademark to shift profits to a 0% regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg imposes an upward transfer pricing adjustment and applies penalties: 10% of the re-characterised amount + late interest at monthly rate 0.6%; if deliberate, the adjustment is treated as a deemed dividend subject to 15% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve thin-capitalised transactions are personally liable for the additional tax and WHT to the extent the company is insolvent; criminal penalties under AO Art. 399 for aiding tax evasion.
